sections.name: 3. Why Product Presentation Matters
sections.title: A product photo is often the closest shoppers get to examining what you sell.
paragraphs: In a physical store, someone can pick up a product, look at its finish, check its size, or turn the packaging around.
Online, they depend on the information and images you provide.
sections.listLead: A basic product photo may identify the item, but it doesn't always answer the questions a shopper has before considering it:
questions: What does the material or finish look like?
Which details make this product different?
What does a particular feature actually do?
How might it fit into the shopper's home, routine, or work?
afterParagraphs: Your product images can help answer those questions.
A close view can make a detail easier to inspect. A relevant in-use image can show where a product fits. A simple visual explanation can make a feature easier to understand.
sections.highlightLine: That gives shoppers more useful information to consider — and gives you more ways to present the product.
sections.closingNote: A designed image cannot guarantee a sale. Its job is to present the product and its relevant details clearly, accurately, and with a visual purpose.
sections.compareNote: A genuine comparison using the exact same product.

sections.name: 4. Different Products Need Different Creative Approaches
sections.eyebrow: DIFFERENT PRODUCTS NEED DIFFERENT CREATIVE APPROACHES
sections.title: The image should help communicate what matters about that product.
sections.intro: A skincare bottle, a kitchen tool, and a piece of furniture don't need the same scene. The right approach depends on the product and what a potential customer may need to understand or notice.

items.title: Show the details people may want to inspect
items.text: When material, finish, shape, or packaging matters, a closer composition and deliberate lighting can make those details easier to see.

image.alt: Genuine product image where lighting and close composition reveal visible details

items.caption: Bring important details into view.

items.title: Show where the product fits
items.text: Some products make more sense when people can see them being used or placed in a relevant setting.
items.text2: A kitchen tool on a counter, a lamp beside a reading chair, or a bag being carried gives more context than an isolated product cutout — when that context accurately represents the product.

items.title: Make a feature easier to understand
items.text: A standard product photo may show a feature without explaining what it does. A focused composition, detail view, or simple annotation can make the point clearer.

items.caption: Make the feature easier to understand.

items.title: Give your product a distinctive visual treatment
items.text: When the same plain product shot is used everywhere, your content can start to look repetitive. A product-appropriate setting, composition, and color treatment can give you another way to present it.

image.placeholder: IMAGE PLACEHOLDER 06 — DISTINCTIVE CREATIVE DIRECTION: Insert a visually distinctive, brand-appropriate product advertisement

items.caption: Create a visual direction that fits the product.

subItems.title: Create more than one advertising angle
subItems.text: Different customers may care about different product qualities. One may focus on convenience; another may care more about appearance, comfort, or a particular feature.
subItems.text2: Creating different truthful visual and copy directions gives you more than one way to communicate the product in your advertising.
subItems.fit: You want creative variations to compare, rather than repeatedly using the same image and message.
subItems.note: We create the creative materials; we don't guarantee which angle will perform best. Results also depend on the offer, audience, price, landing page, campaign setup, and market conditions.

subItems.title: Keep your product content more consistent
subItems.text: When products appear across a store, website, and social channels, unrelated visual styles can make the overall presentation feel disconnected.
subItems.text2: A shared visual direction can help product images and copy feel like parts of the same business.
subItems.fit: You have several products or need content for more than one marketing channel.

subItems.title: Get help with the creative work
subItems.text: Planning an image, preparing variations, writing captions, and updating product descriptions all take time.
subItems.text2: Send us the product information and source materials you have. We'll take care of the creative work included in your order.
subItems.fit: You want help producing product visuals and copy without handling every part yourself.

sections.name: 11. FAQ
sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Answers to common questions about ordering, briefs, files, revisions, and payment.

items.q: What do I need to send you?
items.a: Send your product photos and a short description of what you need. It also helps to include your product details, website or product listing, intended platform, target customer, and any brand references.

items.q: Can I order only one service?
items.a: Yes. You can order a product advertising image, an advertising caption, or a product description individually. You can also choose the combined ad package or build a larger order.

items.q: What is included in the Facebook & Instagram Ad Package?
items.a: The package includes one product advertising image and one advertising caption.

The package builder calculates the discount based on the eligible items in your order. The available discount can increase as you add items, up to a maximum of 50%. Your final price and savings are displayed before checkout.
Typical delivery is 1–3 working days, depending on the number of items and the complexity of the order.
Yes. Two rounds of revisions are included. Revisions should relate to the original agreed brief. A substantially different concept or new scope of work may require a separate order.

items.q: What file formats will I receive?
items.a: Images are delivered as JPG or PNG. Written content is delivered as DOC or TXT.

items.q: Can you make images for my specific platform?
items.a: Tell us where you intend to use the image and provide any required dimensions or specifications. We'll take that information into account when preparing the deliverable.

items.q: Will the images increase my sales or ad performance?
items.a:
We can't guarantee that. Advertising results depend on many factors beyond the creative itself, including the product, price, offer, audience, competition, landing page, and campaign setup.

Our job is to create product visuals and copy that communicate the product clearly and give you creative material to use.

items.q: Do I need to provide an advertising concept?
items.a: No. If you already have a direction, share it with us. If not, tell us about the product and what you want shoppers to notice or understand. We can develop a suitable creative direction within the agreed scope.

items.q: Can you follow my existing brand style?
items.a: Share your website, brand guidelines, or visual references. We can use them to guide the work. Please identify any elements that must remain consistent.
Current payment methods listed are PayPal and bank transfer.

items.q: What if my product photo is low quality?
items.a: Send the photo before ordering if you're unsure. The quality and detail of the source material can affect what's possible. We'll let you know if the image is unsuitable or if better source material is needed.

items.q: Do you work with every type of product?
items.a: Send us the product category and a link or photo so we can assess whether it's a suitable fit. We should confirm suitability before accepting an order involving specialist knowledge, regulated claims, or visual details we cannot reliably reproduce.
